newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Meat, fruit and veg push NZ FPI down in November.
newsitem.headline: Meat, fruit and veg push NZ FPI down in November.

text.p: Cheaper meat, fruit and vegetables pushed the New Zealand Food Price Index down 0.1 percent in November, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.

The annual rise in the index was 2.1 percent, considerably down on the 3.2 percent rise in the October year, mainly because there had been a 1.0 percent rise in the index in November 1995. Prices for meat, fish and poultry in November fell 0.4 percent from October. Most of this was due to falling prices of corned beef, fresh fish and lamb chops. Partially offsetting these decreases were increases in pork, bacon and ham prices.
Meat, fish and poultry prices are now 0.9 percent higher than in November 1995.
Fruit and vegetable prices fell 0.3 percent in November largely due to falling prices of tomatoes, apples and lettuce. Overall, fruit and vegetable prices are 2.4 percent lower than in November 1995.
No change was recorded in the areas of restaurant meals or grocery foods in November. However, ready-to-eat foods were 2.0 percent higher than in November 1995.
November was the first month for a year in which ready-to- eat foods posted a decrease and it was also the first month since June that grocery foods did not increase.
The FPI in the North Island fell 0.2 percent with Auckland and Christchurch prices falling by that amount and prices in Wellington falling by 0.1 percent.
